apo-01-cartas.context: Jesus speaks to real churches under pressure. To Ephesus, he praises and corrects; to Smyrna, poor and persecuted, he encourages faithfulness until death.
apo-01-cartas.focusQuestion: What word from Jesus to his church do you need to hear today?
apo-01-cartas.keywordGloss: Whoever listens to the Spirit, repents, and remains faithful receives the promise of life.
facts: Jesus rebukes Ephesus for leaving its first love.
Jesus calls Ephesus to remember, repent, and return to the first works.
To the one who overcomes, Jesus promises to eat from the tree of life.
Jesus knows Smyrna's tribulation and poverty.
To the faithful until death, Jesus promises the crown of life.

apo-02-cordeiro.context: No one could open the scroll, and John wept. Then the Lamb appears, standing as though slain: victory goes through the cross, and all heaven sings.
apo-02-cordeiro.focusQuestion: Why is the Lamb who was slain worthy to govern history?
apo-02-cordeiro.keywordGloss: Jesus slain and alive, the only one worthy to open the scroll and govern history.
facts: John sees a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain.
The Lamb takes the scroll from the hand of the one on the throne.
The bowls of incense are the prayers of the saints.
The Lamb bought for God people from every tribe, language, people, and nation.
Every creature praises the one on the throne and the Lamb.

apo-03-novo.context: The end is not an escape from creation but a renewal: the new Jerusalem comes down, God dwells with mankind, and tears, death, mourning, and pain pass away.
apo-03-novo.focusQuestion: How does this hope change the way you carry suffering today?
apo-03-novo.keywordGloss: God makes all things new and dwells forever with his people.
facts: John sees a new heaven and a new earth.
The new Jerusalem comes down from heaven, from God.
God will dwell with mankind, and they will be his people.
God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
Death will be no more, nor mourning, nor crying, nor pain.
The one on the throne says he makes all things new.

apo-04-visao.context: Before the letters, John sees Jesus glorious in the midst of the lampstands. The vision is frightening, but Jesus touches John, tells him not to fear, and presents himself as the living one.
apo-04-visao.focusQuestion: When you think about the future, do you first see fear or the living Christ?
apo-04-visao.keywordGloss: Jesus glorious, present in the midst of the churches and victor over death.
reflectionPrompts: Christ in the midst of the church
facts: Jesus' eyes were like flames of fire.
Jesus held seven stars in his right hand.
Jesus tells John not to fear, for he is the first and the last.
Jesus was dead, but he is alive for all ages.
The seven lampstands represent the seven churches.

apo-06-selos.context: After the lists of the sealed by tribe, John sees a multitude that no one can count, from all nations, in white robes before the throne and the Lamb.
apo-06-selos.focusQuestion: In the midst of chaos, is your trust in the Lamb or in the news?
apo-06-selos.keywordGloss: God knows and keeps his own in the midst of tribulation.
facts: Twelve thousand sealed are counted from each listed tribe.
John sees a great multitude that no one could count.
The multitude comes from all nations, tribes, peoples, and languages.
The multitude stands before the throne and before the Lamb.
The multitude cries out that salvation belongs to God and the Lamb.
All the angels fall down and worship God.

apo-07-babilonia.context: An angel announces the fall of Babylon the great, a system of luxury and sin that seduced the nations. From heaven comes the call: come out of her, my people.
apo-07-babilonia.focusQuestion: Where are you complicit in something God has already judged?
apo-07-babilonia.keywordGloss: The seductive, oppressive system that God judges; the people must come out of it.
reflectionPrompts: My people, come out of her
facts: An angel comes down from heaven with great authority and lights up the earth.
The angel announces that Babylon the great has fallen.
All the nations drank of the wine of Babylon's immorality.
The voice from heaven tells God's people to come out of Babylon.
Babylon's sins have piled up to heaven.
Babylon glorified herself and gave herself to luxuries.

apo-boss-01.context: This challenge reviews the letters, the vision of the glorious Christ, and the Lamb on the throne: Jesus shepherds real churches, lives forever, and conquers through the cross.
apo-boss-01.focusQuestion: What does Revelation do with your fear of the future?
apo-boss-01.keywordGloss: The Lamb at the center sustains pressured churches without fear.
facts: Ephesus left its first love.
To the faithful until death, Jesus promises the crown of life.
Jesus was dead, but he is alive for all ages.
The seven lampstands represent the seven churches.
John sees a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain.
The Lamb bought for God people from every nation.

apo-boss-02.context: This challenge reviews the multitude kept by God, the fall of Babylon, and the new creation: coming out of complicity to live with God without death or pain.
apo-boss-02.focusQuestion: How does the hope of the end change your faithfulness today?
apo-boss-02.keywordGloss: History ends with God dwelling with a people from all nations.
facts: The multitude comes from all nations, tribes, peoples, and languages.
The multitude cries out that salvation belongs to God and the Lamb.
The angel announces that Babylon the great has fallen.
The voice from heaven tells God's people to come out of Babylon.
God will dwell with mankind, and they will be his people.
God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
